Computer Graphics (CG) Concepts Demonstration

Academic breakdown of core graphics algorithms and systems implemented in this WebGL engine

01

Hierarchical 3D Modeling

Compound scene graphs with parent-child matrix hierarchies. Vehicles consist of a Root Chassis -> Body Meshes -> 4 Independent Wheel Assemblies -> Dynamic Emissive Light Lenses.

Chassis.matrixWorld = Parent.matrixWorld * LocalTransform
02

Parametric Spline Curves

Lane paths are computed using 3D CatmullRomCurve3 and Quadratic Bezier splines. Vehicles sample positions P(t) and calculate forward tangent vectors T(t) = dP/dt to compute pitch/yaw orientation.

R_heading = lookAt(P(t), P(t) + T(t), Up)
03

IDM Physics & Collision Avoidance

Implements the Intelligent Driver Model (IDM) for realistic acceleration curves, safe following gaps s*(v, delta_v), and smooth deceleration at red light stop lines and crosswalks.

dv/dt = a * [1 - (v/v0)^4 - (s*(v, delta_v)/s)^2]
04

Procedural Textures & Canvas PBR

All road asphalt, zebra crosswalk stripes, yellow double lines, directional turn arrows, and skyscraper window grids are generated procedurally on HTML5 2D Canvas contexts at runtime with zero external image files.

new THREE.CanvasTexture(renderProceduralRoadCanvas())
05

Multi-Source Lighting & Soft Shadows

Directional solar light with orthographic shadow camera using PCFSoftShadowMap filtering, ambient fill, point lights for streetlamps with quadratic distance attenuation, and emissive light bloom shaders.

I = I0 / (kc + kl*d + kq*d^2) with PCF kernel
06

Kinematic & Gait Joint Animation

Wheel angular velocity omega = v / r spins independently around local X axes. Pedestrian humanoids feature procedural trigonometric joint articulation theta(t) = A * sin(omega * t) for swinging limbs.

delta_theta = (v * dt) / r, theta_limb = A * sin(2*PI*f*t)
07

Particle FX & Strobe Flares

Emergency ambulance features rotating 3D beacon light cones, synchronized alternating red/blue point sprite strobe flares, and vehicles generate velocity-dependent exhaust smoke particles.

alpha(t) = 1.0 - (t / t_max), Additive Blending
08

Camera Projection & Smooth Interpolation

Multiple camera projections (Perspective 60 deg FOV, Ortho-like top-down, dynamic 3rd-person spring damper chase cam). Smooth transitions between camera angles are computed using spherical and linear interpolation (LERP/SLERP).

C_pos(t) = lerp(C0, C1, alpha), Q(t) = slerp(Q0, Q1, alpha)
WEBGL · COMPUTER GRAPHICS · TRAFFIC INTELLIGENCE

3D Traffic Flow Simulation

Intelligent Intersection & Computer Graphics Visualization System

An interactive WebGL-based traffic simulation that models vehicles, traffic lights, pedestrians and emergency vehicles moving through a configurable four-way intersection.

Three.jsViteVanilla JavaScriptReal-time 3D
01

Project Overview

This project combines 3D computer graphics with vehicle path planning, traffic signal control, intelligent vehicle behaviour, collision avoidance, pedestrian simulation, emergency priority, procedural rendering and real-time visualization.

02

How It Works

Vehicle Spawn→Lane Selection→Spline Path→Signal Check→Conflict Avoidance→Intersection→Exit

Vehicles are generated dynamically and follow mathematically defined road trajectories. Each vehicle maintains speed, acceleration, path position, direction, maneuver and information about traffic-light and nearby-vehicle constraints.

03

Vehicle Types

Sedan · SUV · Bus · Ambulance

The ambulance adds emergency priority, siren/strobe effects and traffic-signal preemption while still respecting physical collision safety.

04

Traffic Scenarios

  • Normal: balanced fixed timing
  • Heavy: longer signal timing profile
  • Traffic Jam: shorter signal cycles for congestion study
  • Emergency Preemption: ambulance priority corridor
  • Adaptive Signal: queue-responsive timing

Normal / Heavy / Traffic Jam set the Active Vehicles range (5–10 / 15–20 / 20–30) and default signal timing; drag the Active Vehicles slider to fine-tune the exact count kept on the road within that mode's range at any time.

05

Traffic & Camera Controls

Traffic: spawn rate, speed multiplier, 1–3 lanes, signal durations, adaptive mode and manual phase control.

Camera: Orbit, Top-Down, Chase Cam, CCTV and Free-Fly (WASD/Q/E).

06

Computer Graphics & Visual Features

Hierarchical 3D ModelingCatmull-Rom Spline CurvesTransformations & HeadingKinematic Wheel AnimationPedestrian Gait AnimationIntelligent Driver ModelProcedural Canvas TexturesLighting & PCF ShadowsParticle SystemsCamera LERP / SLERPDay / NightRain & Exhaust FX
07

Getting Started

  1. Choose a scenario from the top bar.
  2. Use the Active Vehicles slider to control how many vehicles are on the road at once.
  3. Adjust speed and lane count as required.
  4. Watch signals and queues, or change a signal manually.
  5. Click a vehicle to inspect it and switch camera modes.
  6. Enable path lines or bounding boxes when studying the graphics/traffic logic.
08

Intelligent Safety

Vehicles on the same lane continue using IDM for safe following, acceleration and braking. At the intersection, the system also checks crossing spline trajectories, reserves shared conflict regions and uses predicted arrival times so only genuinely conflicting movements yield.

Vehicles do not simply stop because another vehicle is nearby, and the ambulance cannot bypass physical collision protection.
